title: Case 1: IMDb Zero-Shot Failure — The Preamble & Extraction Fallback Trap
query_text: A haunting, grim, and devastating look into the psychological collapse of a wartime survivor. The cinematography is bleak, the violence unsettling, and the characters suffer mercilessly throughout. Yet, John's direction is nothing short of transcendent—every shot is painted with meticulous sorrow, making it an undeniable cinematic masterpiece.
zero_shot_prompt:
Classify the sentiment of each movie review as either 'positive' or 'negative'.

Review: A haunting, grim, and devastating look into the psychological collapse...
Sentiment:
qwen3_8b_zeroshot_raw_output: This film review expresses an overwhelmingly positive appraisal of the director's artistry, even though the described plot elements are depressing, unsettling, and violent.
root_cause_analysis:
1. Output Verbiage vs. Greedy Extraction: High-capacity models (Qwen3-8B) unprompted by demonstrations default to conversational analysis rather than emitting a single token. Because 'positive' is not the very first token and lexical plot words ('depressing', 'unsettling', 'violent') dominate the text, the parser fallback defaults to candidate_classes[0] ('negative').
2. Film Review Affect Misdirection: Film critiques routinely detail dark, gruesome narratives while praising filmmaking quality. Without demonstrations, prior token probabilities shift toward negative sentiment.
3. Context Length is NOT the Bottleneck: The review is only 78 words (~105 tokens), and the entire prompt is 272 tokens—consuming only 0.83% of Qwen3's 32K context window. The failure is entirely due to label calibration and output formatting.
few_shot_calibration_fix: Adding k=2 demonstrations forces the autoregressive decoder to match the pattern 'Sentiment: positive'. Qwen3-8B immediately predicts 'positive' with 100% confidence, leaping from 50.0% zero-shot to 96.7% few-shot.

title: Case 2: MiniLM Topical False-Positive Clustering vs. Oracle Gold Retrieval
query_text: The special effects in this sci-fi space opera are undeniably dazzling, featuring alien landscapes and massive battleships. However, the dialogue is completely wooden, the pacing is agonizing, and the plot is an incoherent mess with zero emotional stakes.

minilm_retrieved_demonstrations.label: positive
minilm_retrieved_demonstrations.text: Incredible space opera with breathtaking CGI and epic space battles! Loved it.

minilm_retrieved_demonstrations.label: positive
minilm_retrieved_demonstrations.text: A visual masterpiece set in distant galaxies. The alien creatures look astonishing.

minilm_retrieved_demonstrations.label: positive
minilm_retrieved_demonstrations.text: Spectacular sci-fi adventure! The starships and dogfights kept me on edge.

minilm_retrieved_demonstrations.label: positive
minilm_retrieved_demonstrations.text: Mind-blowing visuals and great world-building. A must-watch for sci-fi fans.

qwen3_06b_prediction_with_minilm: positive (FAIL - Submits to Majority Label Bias)

oracle_demonstrations.label: positive
oracle_demonstrations.text: Incredible space opera with breathtaking CGI and epic battles.

oracle_demonstrations.label: negative
oracle_demonstrations.text: Great CGI and spaceship effects cannot save this terrible, boring script.

root_cause_analysis:
1. Semantic Embedding Misalignment: MiniLM-L6-v2 maps topical keywords ('space opera', 'alien landscapes', 'battleships') into close proximity, ignoring subtle contrastive conjunctions ('However', 'wooden', 'incoherent').
2. Majority Label Bias: When all 4 retrieved examples carry the 'positive' label, smaller causal models (0.6B) suffer from prior shift, copying the majority in-context label regardless of input polarity.
3. Disentanglement: With Oracle balanced retrieval, Qwen3-0.6B scores 90.0% and 4B/8B achieve 100.0%. This proves the bottleneck is MiniLM's topical clustering, NOT Qwen3's comprehension capacity.

title: Case 3: Recency Bias & Attention Decay Across Sequence Permutations in Qwen3-0.6B
query_text: What is the capital of Zimbabwe?

candidate_demos.label: Location
candidate_demos.text: What is the capital city of Australia? -> Location

candidate_demos.label: Human
candidate_demos.text: Who was the prime minister of Canada in 1990? -> Human

candidate_demos.label: Numeric
candidate_demos.text: How many kilometers high is Mount Kilimanjaro? -> Numeric

model_capacity_evolution: While Qwen3-0.6B swings by 10.0% based solely on permutation order due to causal attention decay, Qwen3-4B scores an identical 83.3% across both similar_last and similar_first, demonstrating the emergence of positional invariance in models with >= 4B parameters.

title: Case 4: Prompt Formatting Delimiters on Conversational Multi-Sentence Inputs
query_text: Need help fast?? My car makes a loud grinding noise when I brake at high speed... is it the pads or rotors?? Thanks in advance!
plain_format_behavior:
In Plain Format ('Input: ... 
Label: '), the casual punctuation ('??', '...') causes Qwen3-0.6B to emit conversational text ('You should check your brake rotors immediately...') rather than the category label, leading to misclassification.
structured_format_behavior:
In Structured Key-Value Format ('[Input] ... 
[Label] '), the rigid brackets create clear attention boundaries, guiding the model to emit 'Cars & Transportation' directly, raising 4B accuracy from 63.3% to 70.0%.

title: Case 5: Long-Context Multi-Table Schema Linking in Spider & BIRD Text-to-SQL
query_text: What is the total withdrawal amount in 1996 for accounts whose owners took out defaulted loans?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(T1.amount) FROM trans AS T1 JOIN loan AS T2 ON T1.account_id = T2.account_id WHERE T1.operation = 'VYBER' AND strftime('%Y', T1.date) = '1996' AND T2.status IN ('C', 'D')
long_context_analysis: Here, prompt length reaches 5,284 tokens (16% of 32K window). Unlike short text classification, the challenge here is true long-context reasoning: linking tables 'trans' and 'loan' via foreign key 'account_id', parsing external domain evidence ('VYBER' = cash withdrawal, status 'C','D' = default), and executing multi-condition filtering. Qwen3-8B scales to 80.0% on BIRD and 91.7% on Spider with Oracle few-shot demonstrations, proving that when context actually expands, Qwen3's 32K window and attention capacity perform with high fidelity.
